reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational principle of independent causal mechanisms (ICM) posits that each cause generates its effect through a distinct mechanism, which are statistically independent. This allows for causal discovery from observational data by exploiting statistical independence among mechanisms. In GSI, this translates into Bayesian inference where each causal pathway contributes independently to posterior beliefs. Structural causal models (SCMs) formalize these relationships using directed acyclic graphs and functional equations, enabling precise modeling of interventions and counterfactuals. These models support GSE’s state-transition logic by defining how variables evolve under causal interventions. Structure identifiability ensures that causal graphs can be recovered from observational data under certain conditions, providing a bridge between empirical observations and causal structure. The interplay of these primitives enables robust causal reasoning in complex systems.
